newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower after strong week.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower after strong week.

text.p: Swiss shares left record territory and closed 1.32 percent lower on the Swiss Market Index (SMI) on Friday.

Traders said prices were pushed down by a somewhat lower dollar, Wall Street's weak opening and some special situations. There was also some profit-taking after a strong week that brought two record closings.
The blue-chip SMI dropped 63.6 points or 1.32 percent at 4,772.5.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) lost 26.56 points or 0.87 percent at 3,024.62.
Turnover was moderate at 1,9 billion francs.
Roche shares were in the spotlight. A Roche $1 billion convertible note programme prompted speculation it planned a takeover, posisbly targetting French pharmaceutical companies Sanofi or Synthelabo.
But analysts later said Roche, which already has 15 billion Swiss francs in liquid assets, did not need an extra billion dollars to make an acquisition.
"There does not have to be a takeover in the background", one dealer said.
Roche dropped first to 12,060 francs and later recovered to 12,100, still 195 francs below the Thursday close.
Novartis lost 38 francs to close at 1,885. The stock was traded ex-dividend of 20 francs.

Holderbank, the world's leading cement maker, was under pressure after some anlaysts reduced net profit estimates following a company presentation on Thursday, although other analysts were more positive.
SMH dropped 3.37 percent or 28 francs to 802 francs.
Volume leader UBS rose seven francs to 1,341 after reporting the first quarter saw a considerable rise in group profit and cash flow.
